title: 5. Hash Functions
objective: Study-guide review — ICCS423 v2 — L07: Cryptography 1 (Symmetric, Hashing, Encoding): 5. Hash Functions .

items: Variable input → fixed output (e.g., SHA-256 always 256 bits)
Avalanche effect — flipping 1 bit in input changes ~50% of output bits

blocks.text: For n-bit hash, collisions cost ~2^(n/2) operations, not 2^n. So a 128-bit hash gives only 64-bit collision resistance. Hence: 256-bit hash for 128-bit security.
Hash gives you integrity, not confidentiality. Anyone can hash. The verifier can detect change but cannot recover the original.
GPUs hash SHA-256 ~10 billion times/second. For passwords use:
Always salt per user. Pepper optional (HSM-stored).
